summary.headline: Very strong balance sheet, but thin and shrinking profits
summary.takeaway: Tesla has far more cash than debt, so its finances look sturdy. But it keeps only a small share of sales as profit, and some efficiency measures have weakened over the past year.

positives.text: Has about $36.2B more cash than debt (net cash). Debt to equity (debt compared with owners' money) is low at 0.104x.
Interest coverage (profit compared with interest costs) is 9.96x, and the Altman Z-score (bankruptcy-risk score) of 14.8 is in the safe zone.
ROE (profit compared with owners' money) is 3.8%, above the peer median of -18.4%. Net margin of 3.1% beats the peer median of 0%.

watch_outs.text: Keeps only about $3 of every $100 in sales as profit. Operating margin (profit from main business) is 3.35%.
ROIC (return on all money invested in the business) is 5.08%, a modest return on the money the company uses.
Piotroski score (9 checks of financial strength) is 5 of 9. ROA fell from 6.7% to 3.1%, and asset turnover dropped from 0.92 to 0.78.

what_to_watch_next: Next earnings report on 28 Jan 2027: check whether profit margins move up from about 3%.
Whether ROA keeps falling from 3.1% and asset turnover from 0.78 in coming results.
